summary: Michaela Mross works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She earned her PhD from the University of Munich in 2014 and studied at Komazawa University. She held posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Göttingen, and Stanford University.

Michaël Peyrot specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University from 1999 to 2010. He held posts at Leiden University (~2012, 2016) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Bitbol works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Pierre Mills and at Paris Diderot University until 1985. His career includes posts at Linacre College, Oxford (~1995), CNRS (~1997), and École Normale Supérieure (~2009).

Michel Bréal specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at ENS and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1859–1864), Collège de France (1864–1905), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1882).

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at the University of South Africa between ~1987 and ~1999, and held a post there in 1990.

Michel Hulin was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and at Paris-Sorbonne University under Olivier Lacombe from ~1970 to ~1977. He served on the faculty at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier in 1988 and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from around 1990 to 2008.

Michel Lejeune was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Meillet (~1926–1930). He held posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1947), the University of Paris (~1951–1977), and EPHE (~1951–1977).

Michel Mohr specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Geneva (1987–1992), Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at INALCO. He held posts at CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (~1953–1966), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1957–1960), EPHE (~1966–1992), and the Société Asiatique (~1967–1996).

Michel Strickmann specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden, Paris Diderot, and EPHE under scholars including Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Stein. He held posts at UC Berkeley (1978) and the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (1983–1985).
Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a post at the University of Cambridge as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow.

Michele Kerbaker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and was a professor at Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).
Michele Martin is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle Spuler is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2001) and held teaching posts at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington (~2002–2005).

Michiel de Vaan is a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~1998–2002) and held a post at Leiden University from approximately 2002 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He held posts at Taisho University (attested 1978–1980; ~1996–2016), Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014), and the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

Michihiko Yajima is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo in 1981 and held posts there (attested 1992) and at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996), Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006).

Michiko Yusa specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar at UC Santa Barbara (~1976–1983) and served as a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).
